claim: Infants with defects in the interleukin 10 receptor (IL10R) develop very early onset inflammatory bowel disease.
source: Infants with defects in the interleukin 10 receptor (IL10R) develop very early onset inflammatory bowel disease.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established clinical knowledge about IL10R deficiency in human infants.

claim: Signs of colitis are absent in IL10R-deficient mice during the first two weeks of life.
source: although signs of colitis are absent in IL10R-deficient mice during the first two weeks of life, intestinal inflammation and macrophage dysfunction begin during the third week of life
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis and scoring data presented in Figure 1A-B showing no inflammation at 2 weeks.

claim: Intestinal inflammation and macrophage dysfunction begin during the third week of life in IL10R-deficient mice.
source: although signs of colitis are absent in IL10R-deficient mice during the first two weeks of life, intestinal inflammation and macrophage dysfunction begin during the third week of life
evidence: This is supported by histological data in Figure 1, flow cytometry data in Figure 2, and gene expression data in Figure 1D showing inflammatory changes at 3 weeks.

claim: The onset of colitis in IL10R-deficient mice is concomitant with weaning and accompanying diversification of the intestinal microbiota.
source: intestinal inflammation and macrophage dysfunction begin during the third week of life, concomitant with weaning and accompanying diversification of the intestinal microbiota
evidence: This is supported by microbiome analysis in Figure 8 showing diversification during weaning period, and temporal correlation with inflammation onset.

claim: IL10R did not directly regulate the microbial ecology during infant development.
source: However, IL10R did not directly regulate the microbial ecology during infant development.
evidence: This is supported by 16S rRNA sequencing data in Figure 8 showing no significant differences in microbial diversity or composition between Il10rb-/- and control mice.

claim: Macrophage depletion with clodronate inhibited the development of colitis in IL10R-deficient mice.
source: macrophage depletion with clodronate inhibited the development of colitis
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing reduced histological scores and inflammatory gene expression following clodronate treatment.

claim: The absence of IL10R specifically on macrophages sensitized infant mice to the development of colitis.
source: while the absence of IL10R specifically on macrophages sensitized infant mice to the development of colitis
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6 showing colitis development in Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice at 3-4 weeks of age.

claim: IL10R-mediated regulation of macrophage function during the early postnatal period is indispensable for preventing the development of murine colitis.
source: These results indicate that IL10R-mediated regulation of macrophage function during the early postnatal period is indispensable for preventing the development of murine colitis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments including macrophage-specific deletion, clodronate depletion, and phenotypic analysis.

claim: Colonic inflammatory infiltrates could be detected in Il10rb-/- but not littermate Il10rb+/- mice by the third week of life.
source: As shown by H and E staining of distal colonic sections in Figure 1A, colonic inflammatory infiltrates could be detected in Il10rb-/- but not littermate Il10rb+/- (control) mice by the third week of life.
evidence: This is directly supported by histological images and scoring data presented in Figure 1A-B.

claim: By the fourth week, more than 80% of Il10rb-/- mice exhibited moderate colitis with crypt abscesses and crypt hyperplasia.
source: By the fourth week, more than 80% of Il10rb-/- mice exhibited moderate colitis with crypt abscesses and crypt hyperplasia (Figure 1A,B)
evidence: This is supported by histological scoring data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Virtually all Il10rb-/- mice displayed histologic signs of colitis by 8 weeks of age.
source: virtually all mice displayed histologic signs of colitis by 8 weeks of age
evidence: This is supported by histological scoring data in Figure 1B showing high scores in all mice at 8 weeks.

claim: At 30 weeks, 100% of Il10rb-/- mice developed severe subacute diffuse colitis.
source: At the end of this time-series (30 weeks), 100% of Il10rb-/- mice developed severe subacute diffuse colitis (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring data in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Endoscopic imaging and clinical scores revealed severe colitis in 30 week old Il10rb-/- mice.
source: At this age, endoscopic imaging and clinical scores revealed severe colitis in Il10rb-/- mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by endoscopic images and scoring data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Occasional mucosal erosion but not ulceration was observed in 30 week old Il10rb-/- mice.
source: Although not detected in endoscopic examination, occasional mucosal erosion (partial loss of mucosa) but not ulceration (complete loss of mucosa) was observed in 30 week old Il10rb-/- mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on histological examination shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The colon length in Il10rb-/- mice was not shortened compared to control mice.
source: Furthermore, while the colon length in Il10rb-/- mice was not shortened compared to the control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by gross colon images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The colon weights of Il10rb-/- mice were significantly increased (p<0.001).
source: the colon weights of Il10rb-/- mice were significantly increased (p<0.001; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data on colon tissue weights shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Growth arrest in Il10rb-/- mice was not observed until 8 weeks of age.
source: Notably, growth arrest in Il10rb-/- mice was not observed until 8 weeks of age (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is supported by body weight measurements over time shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Growth arrest is an insensitive indicator of intestinal inflammation in the Il10rb-/- mouse model.
source: indicating that growth arrest is an insensitive indicator of intestinal inflammation in this system
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that inflammation is present at 3-4 weeks but growth arrest doesn't occur until 8 weeks.

claim: During the third and fourth week of life, there was a dramatic increase in proinflammatory cytokine expression including Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf within the colon of Il10rb-/- mice but not in littermate controls.
source: Strikingly, during the third and fourth week of life, we observed a dramatic increase in proinflammatory cytokine expression including Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf within the colon of Il10rb-/- mice but not in littermate controls (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR gene expression data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Concomitant enhanced expression of Il10 started at 3 weeks in both Il10rb-/- and control mice.
source: Interestingly, concomitant enhanced expression of Il10 also started at 3 weeks in both Il10rb-/- and control mice
evidence: This is supported by Il10 gene expression data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The induction of IL10 in control mice is necessary to curtail a proinflammatory stimulus that begins in the third week of life.
source: suggesting that the induction of IL10 in control mice is itself necessary to curtail a proinflammatory stimulus that begins in the third week of life
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Il10 expression increases in both genotypes at 3 weeks, but only Il10rb-/- mice develop inflammation.

claim: Colonic CD11b+CD64+ macrophages that exhibited cell surface expression of Ly6C (Ly6C+MHCII- and Ly6C+MHCII+, referred to as P1 and P2 macrophages) expanded to a much greater degree in Il10rb-/- mice than in control mice between the second and third week of life.
source: We found that colonic CD11b+CD64+ MΦs that exhibited cell surface expression of Ly6C (Ly6C+MHCII-, and Ly6C+MHCII+, referred to as P1 and P2 MΦs, respectively) expanded to a much greater degree in Il10rb-/- mice than in control mice between the second and third week of life
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: There was a concomitant decrease in the percentage of Ly6C-MHCII+ (P3/P4) macrophages in Il10rb-/- mice between the second and third week of life.
source: with a concomitant decrease in the percentage of Ly6C-MHCII+ (referred to as population P3/P4 MΦs, gating strategy shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1) (Figure 2A,B)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A-B.

claim: The P1 and P2 macrophage populations represent recently recruited monocytes.
source: Given that the P1 and P2 MΦ populations are thought to represent recently recruited monocytes
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from prior literature about macrophage populations.

claim: The P3/P4 macrophage population represents resident IL10-expressing macrophages.
source: while the P3/P4 MΦ population is thought to represent resident IL10-expressing MΦs (Bain et al., 2014, 2013; Tamoutounour et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on cited literature (Bain et al., 2014, 2013; Tamoutounour et al., 2012).

claim: There is a marked elevation in newly recruited monocytes within the lamina propria of 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice.
source: these results suggest a marked elevation in newly recruited monocytes within the LP of 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice
evidence: This is inferred from the increased P1/P2 populations observed in flow cytometry data.

claim: The total cell numbers of all macrophage subsets (P1-P4) in the colons of Il10rb-/- mice were increased compared to control mice at 3 weeks.
source: Interestingly, while the relative abundance of P1/P2 versus P3/P4 MΦ were distributed reciprocally in 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice compared to control mice, the total cell numbers of all MΦ subsets (P1-P4) in the colons of Il10rb-/- mice were increased compared to control mice (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is supported by absolute cell number quantification in Figure 2B.

claim: The recruitment of monocytes and conversion to macrophages is enhanced within the colonic lamina propria of 3 week old mice lacking IL10Rβ.
source: consistent with the hypothesis that the recruitment of monocytes and conversion to MΦs is enhanced within the colonic LP of 3 week old mice lacking IL10Rβ
evidence: This is inferred from the increased total numbers of all macrophage populations.

claim: Significant differences between infant Il10rb-/- and control mice within lymphocyte subsets were only detected for the proportions of FoxP3+ Tregs and IFNγ-producing effector T cells.
source: Within lymphocyte subsets (Th1, Th17, Treg, ILC3s), significant differences between infant Il10rb-/- and control mice were only detected for the proportions of FoxP3+ Tregs, and IFNγ-producing effector T cells
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The magnitude of difference in FoxP3+ Tregs and IFNγ-producing effector T cells between Il10rb-/- and control mice was relatively small.
source: although the magnitude of this difference was relatively small (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C,E–G)
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There were subtle differences in CD11c+ DC subsets in 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice compared to control mice.
source: Similarly, there were subtle differences in CD11c+ DC subsets in 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice compared to the control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D,H).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D,H.

claim: There are significant perturbations in macrophage phenotype but not other innate or adaptive immune cells within the lamina propria of 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate significant perturbations in MΦ phenotype but not other innate or adaptive immune cells within the LP of 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on flow cytometry data from Figures 2 and 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: P3/P4 lamina propria macrophages exhibit anti-inflammatory properties based on low expression of proinflammatory mediators including IL6, iNOS (Nos2), and TNF, and their ability to secrete IL10.
source: It has previously been suggested that P3/P4 LP MΦs exhibit anti-inflammatory properties, in part based on low expression of proinflammatory mediators including IL6, iNOS (Nos2), and TNF, and their ability to secrete IL10 (Bain et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on cited literature (Bain et al., 2013).

claim: There was no significant difference in expression of proinflammatory genes in macrophages isolated from 1 week old mice of either genotype.
source: Interestingly, while we did not detect any significant difference in expression of these genes in MΦs isolated from 1 week old mice of either genotype
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of proinflammatory genes appeared higher in P3/P4 lamina propria macrophages isolated from 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice than from control mice.
source: expression of this set of genes appeared higher in P3/P4 LP MΦs isolated from 3 week old Il10rb-/- mice than from control mice (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: qRT-PCR validation on FACS-sorted P3/P4 macrophages from 3-4 week old Il10rb-/- and control mice confirmed higher expression of proinflammatory genes.
source: We further validated the expression of a subset of these genes by qRT-PCR analysis on FACS-sorted P3/P4 MΦs from 3-4 week old Il10rb-/- and control mice and found similar results (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: P3/P4 macrophages isolated from Il10rb-/- mice lose their anti-inflammatory signature by 3 weeks of age.
source: These data suggest that P3/P4 MΦs isolated from Il10rb-/- mice lose their anti-inflammatory signature by 3 weeks of age.
evidence: This is inferred from RNA-seq and qRT-PCR data showing increased proinflammatory gene expression at 3 weeks.

claim: Clodronate-containing liposomes significantly inhibited the histological signs of colitis in 3–4 week old Il10rb-/- mice compared to those treated with control liposomes.
source: Clodronate-containing liposomes significantly inhibited the histological signs of colitis in 3–4 week old Il10rb-/- mice compared to those treated with control liposomes (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring data in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Clodronate treatment significantly reduced the abundance of both P2 and P3/P4 macrophages in the colonic lamina propria of Il10rb-/- mice.
source: Immunophenotypic analyses revealed that clodronate treatment significantly reduced the abundance of both P2 and P3/P4 MФs in the colonic LP of Il10rb-/- mice (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Clodronate treatment reduced the percentages and absolute numbers of CD4+ T cells that produced IL17A and IFNγ in Il10rb-/- mice.
source: as well as the percentages and absolute numbers of CD4+ T cells that produced IL17A and IFNγ (Figure 4C,E)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4C,E.

claim: Clodronate treatment led to significantly abrogated expression of genes encoding for proinflammatory effector cytokines including Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, and Il1b in the colons of Il10rb-/- mice.
source: In addition, clodronate treatment led to significantly abrogated expression of genes encoding for proinflammatory effector cytokines including Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, and Il1b (Figure 4F) in the colons of Il10rb-/- mice.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4F.

claim: Lamina propria macrophages are important effectors of colonic inflammatory response in the absence of IL10R signaling in infant mice.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the LP MΦs are important effectors of colonic inflammatory response in the absence of IL10R signaling in infant mice.
evidence: This is inferred from clodronate depletion experiments showing reduced inflammation when macrophages are depleted.

claim: IL10Rβ is a component of receptor complexes including the receptors for IL22, IL26, and IFNλ.
source: However, IL10Rβ is also a component of other receptor complexes including the receptors for IL22, IL26, and IFNλ (Donnelly et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on cited literature (Donnelly et al., 2004).

claim: 100% of Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice developed moderate multifocal proliferative granulocytic colitis with crypt abscesses and loss of goblet cells at 3 weeks.
source: While infant Cdcs1+/+Il10ra+/- mice (control) were asymptomatic, 100% of Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice developed moderate multifocal proliferative granulocytic colitis with crypt abscesses and loss of goblet cells at 3 weeks (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: By 12 weeks, most Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice developed severe diffuse proliferative granulocytic colitis with loss of goblet cells.
source: By 12 weeks, most of the Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice developed severe diffuse proliferative granulocytic colitis with loss of goblet cells (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated but data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: 3 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice displayed increased numbers of lamina propria macrophage populations and a skewing of the frequency towards the P1/P2 populations.
source: Consistent with data from Il10rb-/- mice (Figure 2A,B), the 3 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice also displayed increased numbers of LP MΦ populations and a skewing of the frequency towards the P1/P2 populations (Figure 5C,D)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5C,D.

claim: 3 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice had significantly higher expression of genes for proinflammatory effectors such as Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf than 3 week old control Cdcs1+/+Il10ra+/- mice.
source: Analysis of colonic gene expression also demonstrated significantly higher expression of genes for proinflammatory effectors such as Il12b, Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf in the 3 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10ra-/- mice than observed in 3 week old control Cdcs1+/+Il10ra+/- mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 5E.

claim: IL10R signaling is necessary to prevent the onset of colitis between the second and third weeks of life.
source: These data strongly support the hypothesis that in this model IL10R signaling is necessary to prevent the onset of colitis between the second and third weeks of life
evidence: This is inferred from data showing colitis development at 3 weeks in both Il10rb-/- and Il10ra-/- mice.

claim: IL10R has critical functions that are independent of the related receptors for IL22, IL26, and IFNλ.
source: and has critical functions that are independent of the related receptors for IL22, IL26, and IFNλ
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Il10ra-/- mice (which have intact IL22R, IL26R, and IFNλR) still develop colitis.

claim: At 6 weeks of age, there were gross signs of colitis including thickened colons and poorly formed stool pellets in Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice that were absent within the colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/f mice.
source: At 6 weeks of age, there were gross signs of colitis including thickened colons and poorly formed stool pellets in Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice that were absent within the colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/f mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by gross macroscopic images in Figure 6A.

claim: 100% of 3–4 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice exhibited mild-moderate colonic inflammation.
source: Histologic analysis revealed that the distal colons of 100% of 3–4 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice exhibited mild-moderate colonic inflammation
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: Inflammation in Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice was further augmented by 6 weeks with significantly increased inflammatory infiltrates, hyperplasia, and loss of goblet cells.
source: that was further augmented by 6 weeks with significantly increased inflammatory infiltrates, hyperplasia, and loss of goblet cells
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/f mice were histologically normal.
source: whereas the colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/f mice were histologically normal (Figure 6B,C)
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring in Figure 6B,C.

claim: There was increased expression of inflammatory genes including Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf within the colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice compared to Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/fl mice.
source: Consistent with the presence of inflammation, we observed increased expression of inflammatory genes including Ifng, Il17a, Il1b, and Tnf within the colons of Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice compared to Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/fl mice (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6D.

claim: The absence of IL10Rα specifically on macrophages led to significantly dysregulated lamina propria pro- (P1/P2) and anti-inflammatory P3/P4 macrophage frequency and numbers.
source: Further, the absence of IL10Rα specifically on MΦs led to significantly dysregulated LP pro- (P1/P2) and anti-inflammatory P3/P4 MΦ frequency and numbers (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6E-F.

claim: There were no statistically significant changes in the frequencies or numbers of lamina propria IFNγ+, IL17A+, or IFNγ+IL17A+ CD4+ T cells in 3–4 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice compared to Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/fl mice.
source: However, we did not detect statistically significant changes in the frequencies or numbers of LP IFNγ+, IL17A+, or IFNγ+IL17A+ CD4+ T cells, or FoxP3+ Tregs in 3–4 week old Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice compared to Cdcs1+/+Il10rafl/fl mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL10Rα signaling on macrophages is necessary to protect from intestinal inflammation during murine infant development.
source: Together, these data confirm that IL10Rα signaling on MΦs is necessary to protect from intestinal inflammation during murine infant development
evidence: This is inferred from experiments showing colitis development in mice lacking IL10Rα specifically on macrophages.

claim: IL10Rα modulates the phenotype of lamina propria macrophages in a cell-intrinsic fashion.
source: and that IL10Rα modulates the phenotype of LP MΦs in a cell-intrinsic fashion
evidence: This is inferred from macrophage-specific deletion experiments showing altered macrophage phenotype.

claim: 4 week old Il10rb-/- mice maintained on regular water developed moderate colitis.
source: As expected, 4 week old Il10rb-/- mice maintained on regular water developed moderate colitis (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by histological images in Figure 7A.

claim: 4-week-old Il10rb-/- mice maintained on the antibiotic cocktail or polymyxin B showed a significant reduction in microscopic signs of colitis.
source: Notably, 4-week-old mice maintained on the antibiotic cocktail or polymyxin B showed a significant reduction in microscopic signs of colitis (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is supported by histological images and scoring in Figure 7A,B.

claim: The median inflammatory score was lower in vancomycin-exposed Il10rb-/- mice than in controls, but this difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: In contrast, while we noted that the median inflammatory score was lower in vancomycin-exposed Il10rb-/- mice than in controls, this difference did not reach statistical significance (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is supported by histological scoring data in Figure 7A,B.

claim: The antibiotic cocktail or polymyxin B significantly reduced the expansion of P1-P2 subsets while simultaneously restoring normal proportions of the P3/P4 subsets of macrophages in Il10rb-/- mice.
source: With regards to the influence of microbiota on MΦ phenotype, analysis of colonic LP MΦs showed that the Abx cocktail or polymyxin B significantly reduced the expansion of P1-P2 subsets while simultaneously restoring normal proportions of the P3/P4 subsets of MΦs in Il10rb-/- mice (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The distribution of pro- and anti-inflammatory lamina propria macrophage distribution in Il10rb-/- mice treated with vancomycin was not significantly changed compared to regular water controls.
source: Consistent with histopathological grading (Figure 7B), however, the distribution of pro- and anti-inflammatory LP MΦ distribution in Il10rb-/- mice treated with vancomycin was not significantly changed compared to regular water controls (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C,D.

claim: Treatment of Il10rb-/- mice with antibiotic cocktail prevented the colonic expression of Il10 as well as major pro-inflammatory effector genes including Il12b, Il17a, and Ifng.
source: Furthermore, the treatment of Il10rb-/- mice with Abx cocktail prevented the colonic expression of Il10 as well as major pro-inflammatory effector genes including Il12b, Il17a, and Ifng compared to Il10rb-/- mice that did not receive antibiotics (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 7E.

claim: Treatment with polymyxin B significantly reduced the expression of Il12b, Ifng, and Il10 but not Il17a in Il10rb-/- mice.
source: While treatment with polymyxin B also significantly reduced the expression of these genes except Il17a
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 7E.

claim: Differences in gene expression levels following exposure to vancomycin did not achieve statistical significance.
source: differences in gene expression levels following exposure to vancomycin did not achieve statistical significance (Figure 7E)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 7E.

claim: Microbiota are a key factor that regulate macrophage function and promote colonic inflammation during early postnatal development in Il10rb-/- mice.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that microbiota are a key factor that regulate MΦ function and promote colonic inflammation during early postnatal development in Il10rb-/- mice.
evidence: This is inferred from antibiotic treatment experiments showing reduced inflammation and altered macrophage phenotype.

claim: Gram-negative bacteria likely represent key effectors of the inflammatory response observed in Il10rb-/- mice during the developmental window around weaning.
source: In addition, the specificity of antibiotics indicate that Gram-negative bacteria likely represent key effectors of the inflammatory response observed in Il10rb-/- mice during this developmental window.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that polymyxin B (which targets Gram-negative bacteria) reduced inflammation.

claim: Microbial community diversity increased rapidly from day 17 to day 35 in both Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice as expected during weaning, and then plateaued.
source: Assessment of microbiota diversity by the Chao1 index showed that in both groups of mice (Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/-), microbial community diversity increased rapidly from day 17 to day 35 as expected during weaning, and then plateaued (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by Chao1 diversity analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: No overall differences in microbial community diversity were observed between Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- genotypes over the time series (p>0.05).
source: However, no overall differences in microbial community diversity were observed between genotypes over the time series (p>0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of Chao1 diversity data in Figure 8A.

claim: Shannon entropy analysis did not show any significant differences in microbial diversity between Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- genotypes.
source: Similarly, Shannon entropy analysis (Shannon, 1997) did not show any significant differences in microbial diversity between genotypes (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated but data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Weighted Unifrac-based comparison of the fecal microbial communities demonstrated similar community composition in Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice regardless of genotype.
source: In addition, weighted Unifrac-based comparison of the fecal microbial communities (a measure of beta diversity) in Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice demonstrated similar community composition regardless of genotype (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by weighted Unifrac analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Both Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice acquired Helicobacter sp. (Otu007, mapping most closely to H. ganmani) at day 17 with the relative abundance increasing up to 4 weeks, which remained stable thereafter.
source: We found that both Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice acquired Helicobacter sp. (Otu007, mapping most closely to H. ganmani) at day 17 with the relative abundance increasing up to 4 weeks, which remained stable thereafter (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by OTU abundance data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The relative abundance of H. ganmani remained comparable between both Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice throughout the time series (p>0.05).
source: However, the relative abundance of H. ganmani remained comparable between both Il10rb-/- and Il10rb+/- mice throughout the time series (p>0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of OTU abundance data in Figure 8C.

claim: IL10Rβ does not directly regulate microbiota composition.
source: These findings suggest that IL10Rβ does not directly regulate microbiota composition
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of differences in microbial diversity and composition between genotypes.

claim: Any ecosystem alterations in Il10rb-/- mice are likely secondary to inflammation induced by the pathogen.
source: and any ecosystem alterations in Il10rb-/- mice are likely secondary to inflammation induced by the pathogen
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that microbiota composition is similar between genotypes despite inflammation in Il10rb-/- mice.

claim: It appears unlikely that IL10R is necessary to control dysbiosis.
source: Thus, it appears unlikely that IL10R is necessary to control dysbiosis
evidence: This is inferred from microbiome data showing no differences between genotypes.

claim: It appears unlikely that dysbiosis is necessary to promote colitis in infant IL10R-deficient mice.
source: or that dysbiosis is necessary to promote colitis in infant IL10R-deficient mice
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that colitis develops without detectable dysbiosis.

claim: Rare loss-of-function mutations in IL10, or its receptors IL10RA or IL10RB in humans lead to infantile onset IBD.
source: In this regard, rare loss-of-function mutations in IL10, or its receptors IL10RA or IL10RB in humans lead to infantile onset IBD (Glocker et al., 2010, 2009; Moran et al., 2013; Shouval et al., 2014a; Kotlarz et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on cited literature documenting human genetic studies.

claim: The IL10/IL10R pathway is essential for intestinal mucosal homeostasis and prevention of intestinal inflammation in infancy.
source: suggesting that the IL10/IL10R pathway is essential for intestinal mucosal homeostasis and prevention of intestinal inflammation in infancy
evidence: This is inferred from human genetic data showing infantile IBD in patients with IL10/IL10R mutations.

claim: IL10 is a potent anti-inflammatory cytokine that inhibits proinflammatory and co-stimulatory function in both innate and adaptive immune cells.
source: IL10 is a potent anti-inflammatory cytokine that inhibits proinflammatory and co-stimulatory function in both innate and adaptive immune cells (Ding and Shevach, 1992; Fiorentino et al., 1991; Saraiva and O'Garra, 2010).
evidence: This is based on cited literature documenting IL10 function.

claim: Mice deficient in IL10 or the IL10R on the 129SvEv background develop chronic spontaneous colitis.
source: Like humans, mice deficient in IL10 or the IL10R on the 129SvEv background develop chronic spontaneous colitis (Kang et al., 2008; Kühn et al., 1993; Spencer et al., 1998)
evidence: This is based on cited literature documenting mouse models.

claim: Colitis in IL10/IL10R-deficient mouse models presents after an extended latency.
source: However, because colitis in these models presents after an extended latency, understanding the developmental events early in life that contribute to disease development remain to be defined.
evidence: This is based on knowledge from prior literature about these mouse models.

claim: The IL10 receptor (IL10R) is a heterotetramer consisting of two chains of ligand-binding IL10Rα (IL10R1) and two subunits of signaling IL10Rβ (IL10R2).
source: The IL10 receptor (IL10R) is a heterotetramer consisting of two chains of ligand-binding IL10Rα (IL10R1) and two subunits of signaling IL10Rβ (IL10R2) (Donnelly et al., 2004; Moore et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on cited literature describing IL10R structure.

claim: The IL10R is expressed on cells of both the innate and adaptive immune compartments.
source: The IL10R is expressed on cells of both the innate and adaptive immune compartments
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about IL10R expression.

claim: IL10R on subsets of regulatory T cells and T helper 17 (Th17) cells plays a role in preventing the development of colitis.
source: and a number of studies have highlighted the role of IL10R on subsets of regulatory T cells and T helper 17 (Th17) cells in preventing the development of colitis (Chaudhry et al., 2011; Huber et al., 2011; Kamanaka et al., 2011; Murai et al., 2009)
evidence: This is based on cited literature documenting the role of IL10R on T cells.

claim: IL10R in innate immune cells is required to prevent murine colitis.
source: Recently, we and others have demonstrated a requirement for IL10R in innate immune cells to prevent murine colitis (Li et al., 2015; Shouval et al., 2014b, 2016; Zigmond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on cited literature including the authors' own prior work.

claim: There is excessive accumulation of inflammatory Ly6C+ monocytes within the colons of colitic IL10R-deficient mice.
source: In addition, we have shown excessive accumulation of inflammatory Ly6C+ monocytes within the colons of colitic IL10R-deficient mice
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior published work.

claim: There are defects in the differentiation of both murine and human anti-inflammatory macrophages defective in IL10R signaling.
source: as well as defects in the differentiation of both murine and human anti-inflammatory macrophages (MΦs) defective in IL10R signaling (Shouval et al., 2014b)
evidence: This is based on cited literature from the authors' prior work.

claim: Intestinal microbiota promotes the accumulation of Ly6C+ monocytes within the lamina propria.
source: It has previously been shown that intestinal microbiota promotes the accumulation of Ly6C+ monocytes within the lamina propria (LP) (Bain et al., 2014)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: The microbiota is intimately involved in the development of colitis in many susceptible mouse models including mice lacking IL10 signaling.
source: and there is ample evidence that the microbiota is intimately involved in the development of colitis in many susceptible mouse models including mice lacking IL10 signaling (Kang et al., 2008; Sellon et al., 1998)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: IL10R signaling on intestinal macrophages prevents microbially-driven recruitment of Ly6C+ monocytes and the development of intestinal inflammation.
source: Taken together, these studies imply that IL10R signaling on intestinal MΦs prevents microbially-driven recruitment of Ly6C+ monocytes and the development of intestinal inflammation.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of prior studies cited.

claim: Colitis that develops spontaneously in mice that are completely-deficient in IL10R manifests with a prolonged latency of several weeks.
source: the colitis that develops spontaneously in mice that are completely-deficient in IL10R or that specifically lack IL10R within CX3CR1+ MΦs manifest with a prolonged latency of several weeks
evidence: This is based on knowledge from prior literature about these mouse models.

claim: Colitis in IL10R-deficient mice is strain- and microbiota-dependent.
source: and is strain- and microbiota-dependent (Kang et al., 2008; Kühn et al., 1993; Spencer et al., 1998; Zigmond et al., 2014)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Colitis in infants lacking functional IL10R is an aggressive disease that presents very early in life.
source: Given that colitis in infants lacking functional IL10R is an aggressive disease that presents very early in life (Glocker et al., 2009; Shouval et al., 2014a)
evidence: This is based on cited literature documenting human clinical presentations.

claim: Clodronate liposome treatment has previously been shown to deplete lamina propria macrophages and inhibit the development of intestinal inflammation in Helicobacter bilis infected Rag2-/- mice.
source: To test this hypothesis, we employed clodronate liposome treatment (i.p.) in 3–4 week old Il10rb-/- mice, a treatment that has previously been shown to deplete LP MΦs and inhibit the development of intestinal inflammation in Helicobacter bilis infected Rag2-/- mice (Muthupalani et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: C57BL/6 mice that specifically lack IL10Rα in macrophages (Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice) do not reliably develop colitis.
source: However, C57BL/6 mice that specifically lack IL10Rα in MΦs (e.g. Il10rafl/flLyz2Cre mice) either do not reliably develop colitis (Li et al., 2015)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Il10rafl/flCx3cr1Cre mice develop colitis with a prolonged latency.
source: or do so with a prolonged latency (e.g. Il10rafl/flCx3cr1Cre mice) (Zigmond et al., 2014)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Antibiotics can inhibit colitis that develops in infant IL10Rβ-deficient mice expressing a dominant negative (dn) TGFβRII in T cells.
source: It has previously been shown that antibiotics can inhibit colitis that develops in infant IL10Rβ-deficient mice expressing a dominant negative (dn) TGFβRII in T cells (Kang et al., 2008)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Gram-positive bacteria promote monocyte/macrophage recruitment into the colonic lamina propria during DSS colitis.
source: and further that Gram-positive bacteria promote monocyte/ MΦ recruitment into the colonic LP during DSS colitis (Nakanishi et al., 2015)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Colitis in IL10-deficient mice is attenuated under germ-free conditions.
source: While our studies are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that colitis in IL10-deficient mice is attenuated under germ-free conditions (Sellon et al., 1998)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: IL10-deficient and WT mice exhibit significant differences in microbial diversity and composition.
source: In contrast, it was previously reported that IL10-deficient and WT mice exhibit significant differences in microbial diversity and composition (Maharshak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Loss in microbial diversity followed the increase in intestinal inflammation in IL10-deficient mice, suggesting that dysbiosis was a secondary event to inflammation.
source: Nonetheless, the fact that loss in microbial diversity followed the increase in intestinal inflammation in IL10-deficient mice suggested that dysbiosis was a secondary event to inflammation in the IL10-deficient model (Maharshak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Colonization of germ-free IL10-deficient mice with H. hepaticus and Lactobacillus reuteri but not either species alone led to severe typhlocolitis.
source: Notably, it has been shown that colonization of germ-free IL10-deficient mice with H. hepaticus and Lactobacillus reuteri but not either species alone, led to severe typhlocolitis in germ-free IL10-deficient mice (Whary et al., 2011)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Inflammation in Il10-/- mice positive for Helicobacter sp. is abrogated in mice specifically lacking the TLR signaling adaptor MyD88 in mononuclear phagocytes.
source: The previous observation that inflammation in Il10-/- mice, positive for Helicobacter sp., is abrogated in mice specifically lacking the TLR signaling adaptor MyD88 in mononuclear phagocytes (Hoshi et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Direct pathogen recognition, including that of Helicobacter sp. and potential other colitis-triggering microbes, is important for the development of intestinal inflammation in the absence of IL10R signaling.
source: indicates the likely importance of direct pathogen recognition, including that of Helicobacter sp. and potential other colitis-triggering microbes, for the development of intestinal inflammation in the absence of IL10R signaling
evidence: This is inferred from cited literature about MyD88 and pathogen recognition.

claim: The increase in microbial diversity observed at the weaning transition coincides with the initiation of monocyte recruitment into the lamina propria.
source: The increase in microbial diversity observed at the weaning transition also coincides with the initiation of monocyte recruitment into the LP
evidence: This is based on knowledge about developmental biology and cited literature.

claim: The increase in microbial diversity at weaning coincides with replacement of yolk sac-derived lamina propria macrophages with monocyte-derived macrophages.
source: and replacement of yolk sac-derived LP MΦs with monocyte-derived MΦs (Bain et al., 2014)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Blocking monocyte recruitment by using a CCR2-neutralizing antibody (MC21) inhibited DSS-induced colitis.
source: Interestingly, while blocking monocyte recruitment by using a CCR2-neutralizing antibody (MC21) inhibited DSS-induced colitis (Zigmond et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Genetic loss of CCR2 did not reverse colonic inflammation in IL10-deficient mice.
source: Consistent with this preliminary experiment, it has previously been demonstrated that genetic loss of CCR2 did not reverse colonic inflammation in IL10-deficient mice (Hoshi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Monocyte recruitment was not completely blocked in Il10-/-Ccr2-/- mice, suggesting that there might be alternate and potentially redundant mechanisms of monocyte recruitment.
source: Notably, monocyte recruitment was not completely blocked in Il10-/-Ccr2-/- mice, suggesting that there might be alternate and potentially redundant mechanisms of monocyte recruitment (Hoshi et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: The function of yolk sac and monocyte-derived lamina propria macrophages are quite similar.
source: While it has been previously proposed that the function of yolk sac and monocyte-derived LP MΦs are quite similar (Bain et al., 2014)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: IL10 rapidly inhibits LPS-induced enhancer activation in bone marrow-derived macrophages.
source: We have recently shown that IL10 rapidly inhibits LPS-induced enhancer activation in bone marrow-derived MΦs (Conaway et al., 2017)
evidence: This is based on the authors' cited prior work.

claim: A relatively small number of adoptively transferred IL10R-sufficient macrophages can suppress the development of colitis in Rag2-/-Il10rb-/- mice reconstituted with CD4+ T cells.
source: Although it is clear that IL10R signaling strongly inhibits a group of inflammation-induced genes, the ability of a relatively small number of adoptively transferred IL10R-sufficient MΦs to suppress the development of colitis in Rag2-/-Il10rb-/- mice reconstituted with CD4+ T cells (Shouval et al., 2014b)
evidence: This is based on cited literature from the authors' prior work.

claim: WT macrophages exert a dominant effect over IL10R-deficient macrophages.
source: suggests that WT MΦs exert a dominant effect over IL10R-deficient MΦs
evidence: This is inferred from adoptive transfer experiments cited.

claim: Enterohepatic Helicobacter species have been shown to drive intestinal inflammation in several immunodeficient murine strains.
source: Enterohepatic Helicobacter species have been shown to drive intestinal inflammation in several immunodeficient murine strains (Fox et al., 2011; Kullberg et al., 1998).
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: Rapid developmental changes in intestinal physiology, immune system responsiveness, diet, and the microbiome occur during the first weeks of life.
source: Given the rapid developmental changes in intestinal physiology, immune system responsiveness, diet, and the microbiome that occur during the first weeks of life (Arrieta et al., 2014; Pantoja-Feliciano et al., 2013)
evidence: This is based on cited literature.

claim: The weaning transition appears to induce a series of events that remodels intestinal homeostasis.
source: Thus, the weaning transition appears to induce a series of events that remodels intestinal homeostasis
evidence: This is inferred from the observations about changes during weaning.

claim: The weaning transition activates a pathway whose inflammatory potential is held in check by IL10R signaling.
source: and in the process, activates a pathway whose inflammatory potential is held in check by IL10R signaling
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that inflammation develops at weaning in IL10R-deficient mice.
